children.text: The fishing town of Donsol in Sorsogon province is the birthplace of ecotourism built around encountering wild whale sharks without feeding them. From
November to June
, swim alongside whale sharks in open water with a licensed guide, and at night, take a boat ride along a river that glows with fireflies — a truly special experience.
Donsol is a quiet fishing town at the southeastern tip of Luzon, in Sorsogon province. It drew worldwide attention after it became known around

that whale sharks (locally called butanding) were gathering in large numbers just offshore. As concern grew at the time over the risk of these whale sharks being hunted, the Philippine government banned the capture and trade of whale sharks, and Donsol residents, together with the WWF Philippines and other groups, created a community-based ecotourism program that treats whale sharks as a tourism asset rather than harming them.

What makes Donsol special is that it is "purely wild." Unlike Oslob in Cebu, which feeds whale sharks to gather them in one spot, here you head out to sea by boat and search for whale sharks that move on their own, foraging for food. So there's no guarantee of a sighting, but the thrill of the moment you finally spot a whale shark —
long — gliding by with its mouth open, feeding on plankton in the open ocean, is something nothing else can replace.
Whale sharks gather because the waters of the Ticao Pass off Donsol are rich in plankton. The season generally runs from late
November
to early
June
, with the highest chance of a sighting from
February–April
. Numbers vary greatly from year to year, and some years have seen very few sightings, so it's recommended to stay at least two days during the season to get two chances.

By day, whale sharks; by night, a firefly river cruise; and nearby in the Ticao Pass, diving with giant manta rays — Donsol suits travelers who love marine life and ecotourism. Even weak swimmers can join wearing a life vest, but since you'll be getting in and out of a boat in open water with some swell, basic comfort in the water is needed.
The Donsol story begins on
December 26, 1997

. Footage of diving instructor Romir Aglugub and his group meeting a whale shark peacefully while scuba diving reached the press and WWF Philippines, and as the misconception that the animals harm people was dispelled, serious research and tourism began. In

, Time magazine named swimming with Donsol's whale sharks the "Best Animal Encounter in Asia." Today Donsol is a municipality in Sorsogon province with 51 barangays and about 52,000 residents (51,781 in the
census). On
, the town hall took over a sustainable tourism development plan (
) prepared by the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU), aiming to broaden Donsol from seasonal tourism that depends on whale sharks alone into a year-round destination.

After registering and attending a briefing at the visitor center, you head out by boat, and a licensed Butanding Interaction Officer (BIO) spots a whale shark and gives the signal to enter the water. Jumping in on cue and swimming alongside a whale shark is, without exaggeration, the whole point of a Donsol trip.

blocks.title: Watch the whale shark briefing video

children.text: After registering, you watch a short briefing video and explanation covering rules like keeping your distance and never touching the animal. Knowing the rules well keeps both the whale sharks and people safe.

After sunset, you board a small boat and travel up the mangrove-lined Donsol and Ogod rivers, where thousands of fireflies twinkle in the riverside trees like Christmas trees. Each boat carries 5–6 people and the trip takes about
1 hour
. You need to keep noise and light to a minimum to see the fireflies well.
Manta Bowl in the Ticao Pass off Donsol is a seamount rising from waters about
deep between the mainland and Ticao Island. Giant manta rays gather at its cleaning stations, and with luck you may even see whale sharks, making it a top dive spot. The maximum depth is about
and it is a drift dive with strong currents, so it is recommended for advanced divers; it takes about
2 hours
by boat from Donsol. You can book through the dive shops in Donsol.
Watching the sea turn red at sunset on the Donsol coast lets you feel the charm of a quiet fishing town. Enjoy it with grilled fish at a beachside restaurant.
Try the flavors of Sorsogon and the wider Bicol region: kinunot, made from shredded stingray or fish simmered in coconut milk and malunggay leaves; spicy Bicol Express; and pili nut treats.

blocks.title: Stroll the village by bike or tricycle

children.text: Donsol town and its coastal villages are small and quiet. An early-morning walk while watching fishermen dock their boats and sell their catch shows you the everyday life of a fishing village, not just the tourist side.
A town festival that celebrates and gives thanks for the whale shark season; in
it was held on

. Highlights are a boat parade on the Donsol River, with each boat decked out in a large whale shark painting and flags, and a street parade led by a life-size whale shark model. Dates may change from year to year, so check the latest announcements.

items.title: From Cebu and other departure points

children.text: From Cebu, Cebgo, a Cebu Pacific affiliate, is reported to operate direct flights to Bicol International Airport. Routes and operating days change often, so check before booking. From cities without a direct flight, connecting in Manila is the usual way, and getting around after you land is as described above.
From Manila to Donsol it is about
by road, and even without stops it takes about
12 hours

. You head south into the Bicol region along the Maharlika (Pan-Philippine) Highway, pass Legazpi, and enter Sorsogon province. Because it is a long distance, many people hire a car with a driver or a van, and to make an early-morning tour it is best to arrive the day before and stay in Donsol.
From Donsol town to Dancalan, the coastal village with the whale shark visitor center, it's about
10 minutes
by tricycle, for roughly

. Most resorts are within walking distance or a few minutes by tricycle from the visitor center. The firefly cruise departure point is also reached by tricycle, often arranged by your resort together with round-trip transport.
The whale shark season generally runs from late
November
to early
June
, with the peak sighting chance from
February–April
. During this period, the sea is relatively calm and the weather clear, so tours run reliably.
December–January
and
May
are the early and late fringes of the season, so there can be days without any whale shark sighting.
The Bicol region sees frequent rain year-round, and is affected by typhoons from
June–December
. Strong typhoons in particular sometimes pass through Sorsogon from
September–December
, suspending tours entirely. Outside the season (roughly
July–October
), whale shark tours are either not run or sightings are very unlikely.
The firefly cruise runs year-round, but is best on nights with no rain and a weak or new moon. Manta Bowl diving is generally best from
December
to
May
During Holy Week (usually March–April), visitor numbers rise and boats and lodging fill up quickly. The Butanding Festival, which celebrates the whale shark season, takes place in mid-
May
. Water temperature in
March–May

September 2025

Typhoons Tino (Kalmaegi) and Uwan (Fung-wong) passed through the Philippines one after another. Even early in the season, weather can upset your plans, so check the PAGASA forecast before you leave.

Lodging clusters along the Dancalan coast, where the whale shark visitor center is located. Small, long-running resorts and bungalows line the beach at around
per night, and most are close to the visitor center for an easy early-morning start. During peak season (
February–April
) weekends and Holy Week, rooms fill up fast, so book ahead. You can also stay in Legazpi and do a day trip, but the early departure makes that more demanding.

The food centers on fresh seafood. In Sorsogon and the wider Bicol region, you can easily find kinunot (stingray or fish simmered in coconut milk and malunggay leaves), spicy Bicol Express, and laing (taro-leaf stew). Ask your resort restaurant to grill the fish and squid caught that day, and you'll enjoy a hearty dinner at a reasonable price. Pili nut treats, a Sorsogon specialty, make good gifts.
Well-known options include Amor Farm Beach Resort, a long-running beachfront property (rooms about

per night), and Giddy's Place, which also houses a PADI dive center. Some lodgings and restaurants close in the off-season, so if you go outside the season, check in advance whether they are open. After a tour, most people have lunch at their resort restaurant, and many places grill the day's catch for dinner. Since there is hardly anywhere to take out cash, it is convenient to withdraw money and shop at a mall near Legazpi Grand Central Terminal (such as SM City Legazpi) before heading in.

Whale shark tours start early in the morning and end around noon. Confirm the visitor center's operating hours and the day's boat assignment order with your lodging the night before, and arrive around
Boats are chartered per boat, so even solo travelers can join others at the visitor center. Arriving earlier makes it easier to find people to share a boat with.
The boat fee is non-refundable even if you don't see a whale shark. It's a good idea to plan for two days to get two chances.
Underwater cameras are fine, but flash is prohibited. If using an action cam, be sure to attach a wrist strap.
Donsol has few or unreliable ATMs. Prepare cash in Legazpi to cover registration fees, boat costs, and lodging.
Bring a rash guard and reef-safe sunscreen. The sun is strong and jellyfish can be present.
If you get seasick, take motion sickness medication
30 minutes
before departure. The boat rocks considerably while searching for whale sharks.
The firefly cruise has a lot of mosquitoes. Apply repellent and turn off your phone's flash.
Vans to Donsol run from Legazpi Grand Central Terminal between about
. Plan to arrive at the terminal with time to spare so you don't miss the last van.

The start and end of the season vary from year to year, so a few days before departure, ask your lodging or the Donsol tourism office about recent whale shark sightings. At the start of the season (December–January) and near its end (May), it is best to plan an extra day.
Touching or riding a whale shark is strictly prohibited. Keep a distance of at least
3 m
from the head and
4 m
from the tail, and respect the limit on how many people can be in the water with one whale shark at a time.
Observing whale sharks with scuba gear is banned — only snorkeling is allowed. Flash photography and underwater scooters are also prohibited.
A whale shark's tail movement is very powerful. Don't get close to the tail.
Since you enter the water in open sea, always wear a life vest if you're not a confident swimmer, and stay close to the interaction officer.
The coast guard halts departures during typhoon and strong wind warnings. Build slack into your schedule in case a tour is canceled.
Mayon Volcano was raised to Alert Level 3 on
January 6, 2026
, and entry to the
6 km
-radius permanent danger zone has been prohibited; there are reports that it was lowered to Alert Level 2 in August, but the situation can change. Bulusan Volcano also had Alert Level 1 issued on
March 22, 2026
. If you include either in a connecting itinerary, check the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) announcements before you leave.
Donsol's whale sharks are wild animals that come here on their own, not gathered for people. Following the rules is what lets us meet them again in this sea next year, and ten years from now.
